'''''Racomitrium lanuginosum''''' is a widespread species of [[moss]] found in montane and arctic [[tundra]], the genus Racomitrium is found across the Northern and Southern hemispheres.,<ref name="FNA">{{cite book |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200001318 |chapter=''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' (Hedwig) Bridel, Muscol. Recent., suppl. 4: 79. 1818 |series=[[Flora of North America]] |volume=27 |title=Bryophytes: Mosses, Part 1 |author1=Ryszard Ochyra  |author2=Halina Bednarek-Ochyra |author1-link=Ryszard Ochyra |name-list-style=amp |year=2007 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]}}</ref> however Racomitrium lanuginosum is only found in the Northern hemisphere. It grows as large mats on exposed rock and in boulder scree, particularly on acidic rocks. Its [[leaf|leaves]] have a characteristically [[decurrent]] and toothed [[hair-point]], which gives rise to its regional common names '''woolly fringemoss''',<ref name=BBS>{{cite book|last=Edwards|first=Sean R.|date=2012|title=English Names for British Bryophytes|location=Wootton, Northampton|publisher=British Bryological Society|isbn=978-0-9561310-2-7|issn=0268-8034|series=British Bryological Society Special Volume|volume=5|edition=4}}</ref> '''hoary rock-moss''' and '''woolly moss'''.

==Description==
[[File:Racomitrium lanuginosum (a, 141103-472338) 5682.JPG|thumb|left|The coarsely toothed hair-points of ''R. lanuginosum'' distinguish it from many other species of ''Racomitrium''.]]
''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' grows as "large cushiony mats".<ref name="Fretwell">{{cite web |url=http://www.centralcoastbiodiversity.org/hoary-rock-moss-bull-racomitrium-lanuginosum.html |title=Hoary rock moss • ''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' |work=Biodiversity of the Central Coast |author1=Kelly Fretwell  |author2=Brian Starzomski  |name-list-style=amp |year=2014 |publisher=[[University of Victoria]] |accessdate=October 22, 2014}}</ref> Its stems are up to {{convert|12|cm}} long and irregularly branched.<ref name="Fretwell"/> The leaves are {{convert|3|-|5|mm}} long, {{convert|0.6|-|0.9|mm|2|abbr=on}} wide, [[lanceolate]], pointed and with a strong [[midrib]].<ref name="FNA"/><ref name="Fretwell"/> They end in a long, thin hair-point, with teeth along both sides pointing 40°–90° from the axis of the leaf.<ref name="FNA"/> The hyaline (transparent) margins of the hair-point are [[decurrent]] along the sides of the leaf.<ref name="FNA"/> Especially when dry, these hair-points give the plant a downy appearance, which is referenced in several of the common names for the species.<ref name="Fretwell"/>

[[Sporophyte]]s are rarely produced,<ref name="FNA"/> although they are reported to be abundant in coastal areas.<ref name="Fretwell"/> The capsules are {{convert|1.0|-|1.7|mm|2|abbr=on}} long, smooth and brown, and contain spores, which are 8–12 μm long.<ref name="FNA"/> The form of the hair-points on the leaves of ''R. lanuginosum'' is unique among mosses.<ref name="FNA"/>

===Similar species===
''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' is "one of the few bryophytes familiar to many non-bryologists".<ref name="Bosanquet"/> Other species that may be confused with it include ''[[Racomitrium canescens|R. canescens]]'' and its close relatives,<ref name="Bosanquet"/> ''[[Racomitrium heterostichum|R. heterostichum]]'' and ''[[Hedwigia stellata]]''.<ref name="Fretwell"/><ref name="Schofield"/>

==Distribution and ecology==
''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' grows from [[sea level]] to the [[alpine zone]], particularly among [[boulder scree]] and on exposed rock surfaces. It will also grow in [[tundra]] or [[bog]]s.<ref name="Schofield"/> It is more frequently found on acidic rocks than calcareous ones.<ref name="FNA"/>

''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' has a [[circumpolar distribution]] in the [[Northern Hemisphere]], and is found [[disjunct distribution|disjunctly]] in the mountains of the [[tropics]] and the [[Southern Hemisphere]].<ref name="Schofield"/>

Within North America, ''R. lanuginosum'' is found widely across northern Canada, and extends further south both in the east (to [[Maine]]), and in the west (to [[California]] and the [[Rocky Mountains]]).<ref name="Schofield"/> It is also found in [[Costa Rica]] and in mountainous regions of [[South America]] and [[South Africa]].<ref name="FNA"/>

In the [[Atlantic Ocean]], isolated populations occur in [[Iceland]], the [[Azores]], the [[Canary Islands]], [[Madeira]], [[Tristan da Cunha]] and [[South Georgia Island|South Georgia]]; it also occurs on [[Réunion]] in the Indian Ocean, in [[New Zealand]], [[Hawaii]] and the sub-Antarctic islands [[Deception Island]], [[Kerguelen Islands|Kerguelen]], [[Îles Crozet]], [[Heard Island]] and the [[Prince Edward Islands]].<ref name="FNA"/>

As well as occurring widely across Arctic Asia, ''R. lanuginosum'' is also found in some temperate and tropical mountains on [[Borneo]], [[Java]], [[Sumatra]] and [[New Guinea]].<ref name="FNA"/> In Australia, ''R. lanuginosum'' is restricted to [[Tasmania]] and the highest ground of the [[Great Dividing Range]] on the border of [[New South Wales]] and [[Victoria, Australia|Victoria]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bie.ala.org.au/species/c158f3ad-a13b-4109-a96f-62704d6ee8b7 |title=''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' "(Hedw.) Brid." |publisher=[[Atlas of Living Australia]] |accessdate=October 22, 2014}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' was [[species description|first described]] by [[Johann Hedwig]] in 1801 as ''Trichostomum lanuginosum''. It was moved to its current genus in 1818 when [[Samuel Elisée Bridel-Brideri]] established the genus ''Racomitrium'', and that position was cemented in 1860 when [[Wilhelm Philippe Schimper]] designated ''R. lanuginosum'' as the [[type species]] of ''Racomitrium''.<ref name="Larraín">{{cite journal |author1=Juan Larraín |author2=Dietmar Quandt |author3=Michael Stech |author4=Jesús Muñoz |year=2013 |title=Lumping or splitting? The case of ''Racomitrium'' (Bryophytina: Grimmiaceae) |journal=[[Taxon (journal)|Taxon]] |volume=62 |issue=6 |pages=1117–1132 |url=http://www.rjb.csic.es/jardinbotanico/ficheros/documentos/pdf/pubinv/JMF/2013_Larrain_Taxon_Lumping_splitting_Racomitrium.pdf |doi=10.12705/626.45}}</ref> ''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' is classified in ''Racomitrium'' sect. ''Racomitrium'', a group that also contains the species ''[[Racomitrium geronticum|R. geronticum]]'' and ''[[Racomitrium pruinosum|R. pruinosum]]''.<ref name="Larraín"/>

''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' is known by a variety of [[vernacular name]]s around the world. In the [[British Isles]], it is known as the "woolly fringe-moss",<ref name="Bosanquet">{{cite book |author=Sam Bosanquet |year=2010 |chapter=''Racomitrium lanuginosum'', woolly fringe-moss |page=539 |title=Mosses and Liverworts of Britain and Ireland: a Field Guide |publisher=[[Botanical Society of the British Isles]] |isbn=978-0-9561310-1-0 |url=http://www.bbsfieldguide.org.uk/sites/default/files/pdfs/mosses/Racomitrium_lanuginosum.pdf }}</ref> in Canada as the "hoary rock-moss",<ref name="Schofield">{{cite web |url=http://linnet.geog.ubc.ca/Atlas/Atlas.aspx?sciname=Racomitrium%20lanuginosum |work=E-Flora BC: Electronic Atlas of the Flora of British Columbia |editor=Brian Klinkenberg |year=2014 |title=''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' (Hedw.) Brid., hoary rock-moss (racomitrium moss) |author=Wilf Schofield |publisher=[[University of British Columbia]] |accessdate=October 22, 2014}}</ref> and in [[New Zealand]] as "woolly moss".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.terrain.net.nz/friends-of-te-henui-group/local-mosses/racomitrium-lanuginosum-woolly-moss.html |title=''Racomitrium lanuginosum'' (woolly moss) |publisher=Taranaki Educational Resource: Research, Analysis and Information Network |accessdate=November 15, 2014}}</ref>
